wording: An independent approximation of P03's event model reproduced its central claim only in part. At threshold 0.2, opinions stayed fragmented without events (conflict 0.55 vs Eq. 6 0.26, not supported) and events added only 0.01 (not supported).
confidence: Low-moderate (5 replicates per condition; independent approximation of P03)
counterevidence_limits: Not P03's code: partner count k = 4, symmetric certainty drift and directed random partners are our choices; 1,000 steps; 5 replicates. The mismatch may reflect our implementation rather than P03.
operationalization: Divergence = event-sustained polarisation (SD of opinions)

wording: In a synthetic 60-country, 6-region panel with growing region effects, P11's value-variation measure rose overall (slope +0.002 per wave, after an initial dip from 0.105 to 0.085) while within-region variation fell from 0.102 to 0.042: global divergence and regional convergence can coexist and both measures register it.
counterevidence_limits: The regional drift was built into the generator; this shows the measures behave as intended, not why real values diverged.
operationalization: Global vs regional value variation

wording: With 8 links per step our SIEM re-implementation again did not match P03's Eq. 6 without events (check not supported at both eps) (conflict 0.54 vs 0.26 at eps 0.2; 0.32 vs 0.20 at eps 0.4) while event runs were 0.60 and 0.65 (Eq. 6: 0.60, 0.45). wording: In a bounded-confidence model with opinion redraws, small noise (0.001 per interaction) left opinion spread close to the noise-free value (0.240 vs 0.227 at eps 0.2; 0.162 vs 0.132 at eps 0.3), while heavy noise (0.1) raised it but not to the uniform value 0.289 (0.262 and 0.201; the pre-registered 'near uniform' check was not supported in either run): noise maintains dispersion without removing homophily's pull.
counterevidence_limits: Noise rule is the agent's choice (unsourced); SD only.
operationalization: Divergence = dispersion maintained by noise

wording: A negative catch-up slope does not show convergence: in a stationary AR(1) toy the growth-on-initial-level slope was -0.64 (expected rho^T - 1 = -0.64) while cross-unit dispersion stayed constant (ratio 1.001); only when initial dispersion was twice the stationary value did dispersion actually shrink (ratio 0.59) with the same slope. Divergence and convergence claims should be stated in dispersion terms (as P11 does with SDs) rather than inferred from slopes.
counterevidence_limits: Statistical toy, not an economic model; no source on beta/sigma convergence read.
operationalization: Divergence/convergence = change in dispersion, not regression slope
